about: Pirate havens (the Ledger topic 'Trade', your answer 'Pirate havens that raid shipping and coasts until suppressed'). Each raids sea trade and coasts within reach_km of its haven from 'from' until history's suppression ('until'), unless a realm suppresses it sooner: by holding the haven, or by keeping warships there for six months. Sources: Polybius 2.8-12 (the Illyrians of Teuta; Rome's wars of 229 and 219 BC; their end in 168 BC, Livy 45.26); Plutarch, Pompey 24-28 and Appian, Mithridatic Wars 92-96 (the Cilician pirates, swept from the sea by Pompey in 67 BC); Diodorus 40.1 and Velleius 2.34 (Crete, conquered by Metellus 69-67 BC); the Barbary corsairs of Algiers, Tunis and Tripoli (about 1500 to the French taking of Algiers in 1830). Our own data, free for any use. 'might' is the pirates' naval strength when they appear (your answer 'Need enough warships'): it grows by 1% a year while no one checks them, up to three times; warships patrolling a haven count only if their naval Might in reach is at least the pirates'. A suppressed haven returns 40 years later, at its first strength, unless the realm holding its coast keeps warships there at least as strong as the pirates once were (your note 'Suppressed havens return later also').
